brief.subject: Dementia and gun safety; what the midterms mean for Medicare
brief.headline: Gun Safety When Dementia Appears, and Medicare After the Midterms
brief.dek: Experts push firearm safety for older gun owners showing cognitive decline, while a new Congress revives debate over Medicare for All.
brief.lede: Public health experts are working on ways to promote firearm safety among older gun owners, especially when there are early signs of dementia.

sections.heading: Dementia Raises Firearm Safety Questions
bullets: Public health experts are developing ways to encourage safe gun practices among older adults who own firearms.
Their focus sharpens when a gun owner shows signs of cognitive decline, a concern many family caregivers face.
Families worried about a loved one's memory and gun access can raise the topic with that person's doctor.

sections.heading: New Congress, Old Medicare Debate
bullets: Democrats took control of Congress in the midterms, helped by voter frustration over healthcare costs, KFF Health News reports.
That shift has renewed talk of Medicare for All, but Democratic control does not guarantee it will pass.
For now, nothing in the report signals an immediate change to current Medicare benefits.

brief.seo_description: Experts promote gun safety for older adults with early dementia signs, and the midterms reopen the Medicare for All debate.

items.title: When a Gun Owner Shows Early Signs of Dementia
items.snippet: Public health experts are finding ways to encourage firearm safety practices for older adults who own guns, especially when there are indications of cognitive decline.

items.title: Midterm Wave Sets a Course for ‘Medicare for All’ Fight
items.snippet: Voter frustration with healthcare costs helped fuel the Democrats’ midterm takeover of Congress. But Democratic control doesn’t mean “Medicare for All” will follow, as some hoped.
